learning_objective: 🎯 Level up your data skills! Learn how to find the 'center' of your data and interpret what graphs are truly trying to tell you about the real world.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The Mean is the average. If you have 5 test scores, you add them all up and divide by 5. It's great, but one extremely high or low score (an outlier) can heavily skew the result!
The Median is the exact middle number when you line all the data up from smallest to largest. If there's an even number of data points, you average the two in the middle. It ignores extreme outliers!
The Mode is simply the number that appears the most often in a dataset. A dataset can have one mode, no mode, or even multiple modes. It's the 'popular vote'.

Data analysis isn't just about math; it's about drawing conclusions. By looking at trends in graphs, we can make decisions—like a shop owner predicting they need to stock more umbrellas in July based on past rain data.

fun_activity.title: ⚖️ The Outlier Experiment
fun_activity.instructions: Take the numbers 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6. Calculate the Mean (it's 4) and Median (it's 4). Now change the number 6 to 100! Calculate them again. The Mean shoots up to 22.8, but the Median stays at 4! This is why Medians are safer for data with crazy outliers (like income).

exam_tips: 📌 Always remember to sort your data from smallest to largest BEFORE finding the Median. If you don't sort it, your answer will be completely wrong!
📌 When asked to find the mean of raw data, the formula is: $\text{Mean} = \frac{\text{Sum of all observations}}{\text{Total number of observations}}$.
📌 If a dataset has two numbers right in the middle (when 'n' is even), the Median is the average of those two numbers.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Mean, Median, and Mode are all different ways to find the 'center' or typical value of a dataset.
⭐ The Mean is heavily affected by extreme outliers, whereas the Median is resilient to them.
⭐ Analyzing data helps us uncover hidden trends and make logical predictions.
